STATUS: ANSWER
The -l, --merge-logic option sets how several annotation values are handled when multiple regions overlap a single record: first, append, append-missing, unique, sum, avg, min or max [bcftools_manual#h019]. It is intended for BED or TAB-delimited annotation files, works only when REF and ALT or BEG and END columns are present, and is an experimental feature [bcftools_manual#h019]. Multiple rules can be given as a comma-separated list or by repeating the option [bcftools_manual#h019]. In a columns file, the merge logic can be given as an extra field on each row [bcftools_manual#h017].

STATUS: ANSWER
Both snpEff and VEP predict variant effects. snpEff annotates and predicts the effects of variants on genes, and its generated VCF header contains the software version and the command line used [sarek_output#h059]. VEP determines the effects of many variant types; its VCF header contains the software version and the version numbers of additional databases such as Clinvar or dbSNP, and it describes the format of the consequence annotations in the INFO field [sarek_output#h060].

STATUS: ANSWER
The context calls Oncotator an older functional annotation tool from The Broad Institute. It states that Funcotator and Oncotator are fundamentally different tools with some similarities, and that a direct comparison should not be made [gatk_funco_tutorial#h031]. Funcotator is described as a functional annotation tool in the core GATK toolset, designed for both somatic and germline use cases [gatk_mutect2_wdl#h002]. The sources do not state which tool is newer, and the comparison tables mentioned in the tutorial are not included in the provided material.

STATUS: ANSWER
Two tools in the context check sample identity. NGSCheckMate determines whether samples come from the same individual using a set of commonly heterozygous SNPs, which helps detect sample mislabelling; its output includes a matched-comparisons file and a dendrogram [sarek_output#h066]. bcftools gtcheck checks sample identity: with -g, query samples are checked against the samples in the -g file, and without -g a multi-sample cross-check is performed [bcftools_manual#h057]. The discordance score equals the number of mismatching genotypes only when GT-vs-GT matching is performed [bcftools_manual#h057].

STATUS: ANSWER
Use build_docker_remote.sh, which creates the full GATK4 image using Google Cloud Build remotely [gatk_docker#h001]. First set your project with gcloud config set project <PROJECT>, choosing a project that has access to Cloud Build [gatk_docker#h001]. Example: export GITHUB_TAG=4.2.6.1, then sudo bash build_docker_remote.sh -e ${GITHUB_TAG} -d ${STAGING_DIR} [gatk_docker#h004]. The image is tagged as us.gcr.io/broad-dsde-methods/broad-gatk-snapshots/gatk-remote-builds:<USERNAME>-<GITHUB_TAG>-<GIT_HASH> [gatk_docker#h001].

STATUS: ANSWER
The tutorial dataset is tiny, so some annotations have insufficient data or no variance, and the usual approach of using a large set of annotations does not suit it [sarek_vc_sarek#h007]. The tutorial therefore limits VQSR to a subset of annotations, set through the process descriptors: -an QD -an MQ -an FS -an SOR for SNPs and -an QD -an FS -an SOR -an DP for INDELs [sarek_vc_sarek#h007]. The tutorial also has only 2 samples, so soft filtering offers no significant improvement and VQSR on such a dataset causes issues with some annotations [sarek_vc_sarek#h003].

STATUS: ANSWER
vcfanno annotates a VCF with any number of INFO fields from any number of VCFs. It uses a simple configuration file that specifies the source annotation files and fields and how they are added to the query VCF [rare_output#h023].

STATUS: ANSWER
The sources do not list the FORMAT fields that bcftools call emits per sample. They only say that the -G option requires per-sample FORMAT/QS or FORMAT/AD tags generated with bcftools mpileup -a QS (or -a AD) [bcftools_manual#h026]. A plugin is invoked as bcftools [plugin NAME|+NAME] '[OPTIONS] FILE -- [PLUGIN OPTIONS]' [bcftools_manual#h095]. Plugins are used like normal commands with the name prefixed by a plus sign, and most accept common options, then a separator, then plugin-specific options; some plugins accept no common options and have their own parameters [bcftools_manual#h095].

STATUS: ANSWER
The GATK jar is located at /gatk/gatk.jar inside the GATK4 Docker image [gatk_docker#h002]. The script build_docker_remote.sh creates the full GATK4 image remotely using Google Cloud Build [gatk_docker#h001].

STATUS: ANSWER
Install git-lfs and run git lfs install, then run git lfs pull from the root of your GATK git clone; the download is about 5 gigabytes [gatk_readme#h025] [gatk_readme#h002]. A full git clone is needed because the git-lfs files in src/main/resources/large are packaged inside the GATK jar and used by tools at runtime, and the zipped source code alone is not buildable [gatk_readme#h008]. The large test data under src/test/resources/large is required only by the test suite, not for building [gatk_readme#h008].

Seven HAS_THRESHOLD links are shown: SOR_gt_3 [G:Threshold:SOR_gt_3], FS_gt_200_indel [G:Threshold:FS_gt_200_indel], FS_gt_60_snp [G:Threshold:FS_gt_60_snp], MQRankSum_lt_-12.5 [G:Threshold:MQRankSum_lt_-12.5], MQ_lt_40 [G:Threshold:MQ_lt_40], QD_lt_2 [G:Threshold:QD_lt_2] and ReadPosRankSum_lt_-8 [G:Threshold:ReadPosRankSum_lt_-8]. The graph notes that one more neighbour was omitted, so the total number of thresholds cannot be confirmed from the sources.

The -l, --merge-logic option sets how multiple annotation values are combined when several regions overlap a single record and the value is written to the tag [bcftools_manual#h019]. Its rules are first (keep the first value), append (allow duplicates), append-missing (also append dots), unique (drop duplicates), sum and avg (numeric fields only), and min or max [bcftools_manual#h019]. It is intended for BED or tab-delimited annotation files, takes effect only when REF and ALT or BEG and END columns are present, and is an experimental feature [bcftools_manual#h019].
